comparative_performance: Hold-boundary change only; no sizing, timing, model, cost or execution-parameter change. On the honest S&P 500 point-in-time universe at 25 bp, 20 offsets, medians, holding at A earned 17.1% a year at worst drawdown -34.7% and Sharpe 1.00, against the B hold's 14.4%, -38.3% and 0.87; SPY earned 13.9%, -33.7% and 0.83, and QQQ 19.0%, -35.1% and 0.91. The A hold is the only tested arm that reaches the program's Sharpe-at-least-1.0 objective on that universe; it beats SPY on CAGR and Sharpe (17.1% against 13.9%, 1.00 against 0.83) while its worst drawdown is 1.0 point deeper (-34.7% against -33.7%). It trails QQQ's raw CAGR while beating QQQ's Sharpe and drawdown. On the live 94-name book in the same regrade scorecard it gives up 1.6 points of CAGR (25.0% against 26.6%) at the same Sharpe 1.11 and a 0.7-point deeper drawdown (-34.1% against -33.4%); that is the disclosed cost of the honest-universe robustness. Walk-forward, the A hold makes 18.3% at 0.98 on the S&P 500 against equal votes' 16.0% at 0.88, and 23.8% at 0.95 on the book against 19.6% at 0.82. The joint configuration's exact scorecard is the A-cut study plus the P/E-history tilt's separate evidence (docs/research/pe-history-tilt-2026-10-24.md); the two were not scored together. There is no formal significance test and no forward record; the scorecard is in-sample research, not forward proof. The 252-session forward record restarts under grade-led-leader-weight/2.
